_note: Guidance only. Every figure here is a rule of thumb for tenants, not legal advice. Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland have their own laws and are marked with differs: true.

roomTemplates.label: Studio
roomTemplates.detail: One main room with a kitchen area

roomTemplates.label: 1-bed flat or house
roomTemplates.detail: Separate bedroom, living room and kitchen

roomTemplates.label: Shared house
roomTemplates.detail: Your room plus the shared spaces

prompts.label: Door
prompts.hint: Stand back and get the whole door and frame. Then the other side. Check the handle and lock.

prompts.label: Walls
prompts.hint: One photo per wall, corner to corner. Get marks, holes and paint patches in shot.

prompts.label: Floor
prompts.hint: Carpet or floor from the doorway, then any stains or wear up close.

prompts.label: Ceiling
prompts.hint: Point up. Look for damp patches, cracks and the light fitting.

prompts.label: Windows
prompts.hint: Glass, frames, sills, locks, blinds or curtains. Check for mould in the corners.

prompts.label: Fixtures and appliances
prompts.hint: Sockets, switches, radiators, the oven, fridge, taps, furniture. Open the oven and fridge.

prompts.label: Anything damaged?
prompts.hint: Close-ups of every mark, chip, stain, burn or crack. Put a coin or key next to it for scale. Add a note saying what it is.

meters.label: Electricity
meters.hint: Photograph the whole display so the numbers and the serial number are clear.

meters.label: Gas
meters.hint: Get the black or white numbers. Ignore any red numbers after the decimal point.

meters.label: Water
meters.hint: Water meters are often outside under a small cover, or under the kitchen sink.

meterOCR._note: Reading guesses must have 4 to 7 whole digits. Serial numbers are usually longer, and 4-digit numbers that look like years are ignored.

dps.name: Deposit Protection Service (DPS)
dps._note: Dispute window: check on the DPS website; 3 months from the end of the tenancy is the usual limit.
dps.plain: The DPS is a government-approved scheme for England and Wales. It can hold the money itself (custodial) or insure it. Its dispute service is free.
steps: Ask your landlord in writing for your deposit back. Say how much you think you should get.
If you agree on part of it, ask for that part now. Once you agree, it should be paid within 10 days.
If you still disagree, raise a dispute on the DPS website. Do it within 3 months of the tenancy ending.
Upload your evidence pack: the move-in record, the email you sent on move-in day, your move-out photos and any messages.
An adjudicator decides using the written evidence from both of you. There is no hearing.
The dispute service needs you both to take part. If it can't be used, the other route is the small claims court.

tds.name: Tenancy Deposit Scheme (TDS)
tds._note: Dispute window: check on the TDS website; 3 months from the end of the tenancy is the usual limit.
tds.plain: TDS is a government-approved scheme for England and Wales, with custodial and insured options. Its dispute service is free.
steps: Ask your landlord in writing for your deposit back. Say how much you think you should get.
If you agree on part of it, ask for that part now. Once you agree, it should be paid within 10 days.
If you still disagree, raise a dispute with TDS online. Do it within 3 months of the tenancy ending.
Send your evidence pack: the move-in record, the email you sent on move-in day, your move-out photos and any messages.
An adjudicator looks at the evidence from both sides and decides. There is no hearing.
If the dispute service can't be used, the other route is the small claims court.

mydeposits.name: mydeposits
mydeposits._note: Dispute window: check on the mydeposits website; 3 months from the end of the tenancy is the usual limit.
mydeposits.plain: mydeposits is a government-approved scheme for England and Wales, with custodial and insured options. Its dispute service is free.
steps: Ask your landlord in writing for your deposit back. Say how much you think you should get.
If you agree on part of it, ask for that part now. Once you agree, it should be paid within 10 days.
If you still disagree, raise a dispute with mydeposits online. Do it within 3 months of the tenancy ending.
Upload your evidence pack: the move-in record, the email you sent on move-in day, your move-out photos and any messages.
An adjudicator decides using the written evidence from both of you.
If the dispute service can't be used, the other route is the small claims court.

unknown.name: Not sure yet
unknown.plain: In England and Wales your deposit should be in one of three schemes: DPS, TDS or mydeposits. Your landlord should have told you which.
steps: Look for the 'prescribed information' your landlord sent. It names the scheme.
If you can't find it, ask your landlord or agent in writing which scheme holds your deposit.
You can also search each scheme's website with your details: DPS, TDS and mydeposits.
If it isn't in any of them, it may not be protected. Get free advice from Shelter or Citizens Advice.

england.label: England
england.law: Housing Act 2004 and Tenant Fees Act 2019
england.penalty: If it isn't protected in time, a court can order the landlord to pay you 1 to 3 times the deposit.
england.returnPlain: Once you and your landlord agree how much you get back, it should be returned within 10 days.

cap.plain: Under the Tenant Fees Act 2019 a deposit can be no more than 5 weeks' rent if the yearly rent is under £50,000, or 6 weeks' rent if it is £50,000 or more.

wales.label: Wales
wales.differsNote: Wales has its own law: the Renting Homes (Wales) Act 2016 and the Renting Homes (Fees etc.) (Wales) Act 2019. Deposits still go in DPS, TDS or mydeposits within 30 days, but there is no legal cap on the security deposit.
wales._note: Wales: no statutory cap on security deposits and the 10-day return comes from scheme rules. Needs checking against gov.wales.
wales.penalty: If it isn't protected in time, a court can order the landlord to pay you up to 3 times the deposit.
wales.returnPlain: Once you agree how much you get back, schemes expect it to be returned within 10 days.

cap.plain: Wales doesn't set a legal cap on the security deposit. A holding deposit can be no more than 1 week's rent.

scotland.label: Scotland
scotland.differsNote: Scotland has its own law and its own schemes: SafeDeposits Scotland, Letting Protection Service Scotland and MyDeposits Scotland. Deposits must be protected within 30 working days of the tenancy starting, and can be no more than 2 months' rent.
scotland._note: Scotland: 30 working days, 2-month cap, up to 3x penalty. Dispute windows differ by scheme and need checking.
scotland.penalty: If it isn't protected in time, a tribunal can order the landlord to pay you up to 3 times the deposit.
scotland.returnPlain: Ask your scheme for the deposit back at the end of the tenancy. Check your scheme's own timescales.

cap.plain: In Scotland a deposit can be no more than 2 months' rent.

scotland.schemesNote: Scottish schemes: SafeDeposits Scotland, Letting Protection Service Scotland, MyDeposits Scotland.

northernIreland.label: Northern Ireland
northernIreland.differsNote: Northern Ireland has its own law and schemes: TDS Northern Ireland and mydeposits Northern Ireland. Deposits must be protected within 28 days, and for tenancies from April 2023 can be no more than 1 month's rent.
northernIreland._note: NI: 28 days, 1-month cap for tenancies from 1 April 2023 (Private Tenancies Act (NI) 2022). Needs checking against nidirect.
northernIreland.penalty: If it isn't protected in time, the council can fine the landlord up to 3 times the deposit.
northernIreland.returnPlain: Ask your scheme for the deposit back at the end of the tenancy. Check your scheme's own timescales.

cap.plain: For tenancies that began from April 2023, a deposit can be no more than 1 month's rent.

northernIreland.schemesNote: Northern Ireland schemes: TDS Northern Ireland, mydeposits Northern Ireland.

legalPoints.title: Protected within 30 days
legalPoints.detail: Your landlord must put your deposit in a government-approved scheme within 30 days of getting it.

legalPoints.title: Prescribed information
legalPoints.detail: In the same 30 days they must tell you which scheme it is in, how to get it back and what to do if you disagree. This is called the prescribed information.

legalPoints.title: If they didn't
legalPoints.detail: If the deposit wasn't protected, or you weren't given the information, a court can order the landlord to pay you 1 to 3 times the deposit. It can also limit how they end the tenancy.

legalPoints.title: Back within 10 days of agreeing
legalPoints.detail: Once you and your landlord agree how much you get back, it should be returned within 10 days.

legalPoints.title: Deposit cap
legalPoints.detail: A deposit can be no more than 5 weeks' rent if the yearly rent is under £50,000, or 6 weeks' rent if it is £50,000 or more.

legalPoints.title: Tenant Fees Act 2019
legalPoints.detail: Most other fees are banned in England. A holding deposit can be no more than 1 week's rent.

legalPoints.title: Fair wear and tear
legalPoints.detail: Landlords shouldn't charge for normal wear from living there. Schemes look at how old things were, how long you lived there and what the check-in record shows.

legalPoints.title: Who has to show it
legalPoints.detail: In a scheme dispute it is usually up to the landlord to show why money should be kept. Dated photos from both ends of the tenancy help the adjudicator see what changed.

legalPoints.title: The free dispute service
legalPoints.detail: Each scheme has a free dispute service. You both usually need to take part. If not, the other route is the small claims court.

legalPoints.title: Scotland is different
legalPoints.detail: Deposits must be protected within 30 working days with SafeDeposits Scotland, Letting Protection Service Scotland or MyDeposits Scotland, and can be no more than 2 months' rent.

legalPoints.title: Northern Ireland is different
legalPoints.detail: Deposits must be protected within 28 days with TDS Northern Ireland or mydeposits Northern Ireland. For tenancies from April 2023 they can be no more than 1 month's rent.

legalPoints.title: Wales is different
legalPoints.detail: Wales follows the Renting Homes (Wales) Act 2016. The English deposit cap doesn't apply, but a holding deposit can be no more than 1 week's rent.

cleaningChecklist.text: Oven, hob and grill degreased, racks and trays too
Fridge and freezer emptied, defrosted and wiped
Cupboards and drawers emptied and wiped out
Sink, taps and worktops clean, no limescale
Limescale off taps, shower head and screen
Mould wiped off sealant and tiles
Floors hoovered and mopped, under the bed too
Skirting boards, doors and light switches wiped
Blu-Tack and hooks removed gently, marks wiped
All your things gone, nothing left in cupboards
Garden and bin area as they were at check-in
All keys together and ready to hand back
